PDS Health-supported Dentists Provided 4,000 Procedures, Expanding Access to Dental Care and Helping Patients Facing Barriers to Treatment
HENDERSON, Nev., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PDS Health® a leading integrated healthcare support organization in the U.S., reached a milestone in serving communities across the nation, providing $1.7 million in donated treatment through its 21-year partnership with national nonprofit Dental Lifeline Network (DLN). Since 2005, PDS Health-supported dentists have expanded access to access to dental care for people with disabilities, older adults and individuals who are medically fragile through DLN's Donated Dental Services program.
As of mid-2026, PDS Health-supported dentists have provided more than 4,000 procedures through the partnership, ranging from exams and X-rays to periodontal treatment and restorative care. The partnership connects patients who cannot afford or otherwise access needed treatment with volunteer dentists who provide care in their practices. PDS Health-supported dentists have served patients in 15 states, with the largest numbers in Colorado, where DLN is headquartered, and in California and Arizona. Today, 89 supported dentists, including 76 general dentists and 13 specialists, volunteer through the program.
"Our partnership with Dental Lifeline Network helps dentists reach people who might otherwise go without the care they need," said Carli Casey, Director, Corporate Social Responsibility at PDS Health. "For more than 20 years, supported dentists and their teams have volunteered their time and expertise to restore patients' oral health and improve their quality of life. Their commitment to service reflects our shared purpose of creating healthier, happier patients."
For many patients served through DLN's Donated Dental Services program, age, disability or medical conditions can make accessing dental care especially difficult. Medicare has historically excluded most dental care from coverage, and adult dental benefits under Medicaid vary widely by state, leaving some patients with limited coverage for the treatment they need. Among patients treated by PDS Health-supported dentists through the partnership, 54% were age 65 or older, 25% required urgent dental treatment at their physician's direction and 14% are military veterans.
This year, the partnership connected U.S. Army veteran Alan Frickx with Jennifer Brown, DMD, practicing dentist and owner of Spring Valley Modern Dentistry in Las Vegas, where he began treatment to improve his oral health and overall health. Dr. Brown's team provided donated fillings and extractions, and Alan is now in the final steps of receiving upper and lower partial dentures.
"I'm so grateful for being chosen for this opportunity," said Frickx. "It's life-changing for me. I'm looking forward to being able to enjoy food and smile again."
"Oral healthcare remains out of reach for millions of Americans. For vulnerable adults—especially those living with severe disabilities or complex medical conditions—these barriers often leave these individuals helpless. Thankfully, with the help of our partner, PDS Health, we are able to help more people get the life-changing care they need." Lynda MacDonald, president and CEO.
The partnership is part of PDS Health's longstanding commitment to supporting clinicians as they serve their communities and help more people access essential oral healthcare.
To learn more, visit pdshealth.com.
About PDS Health
PDS Health® continues the journey started by Pacific Dental Services® in 1994, with a vision to redefine healthcare through the integration of dental and medical services. Its approach, centered on the connection between oral health and overall health, aims to create healthier, happier patients and set new benchmarks in the healthcare industry. As a leading provider of integrated healthcare support, the company delivers a broad spectrum of services to dental, dental specialties, and medical providers, enhancing operations and care delivery for clinicians across the U.S. For more information about PDS Health, visit pdshealth.com. 
About Dental Lifeline Network
Dental Lifeline Network (DLN) is a nonprofit organization that connects qualifying elderly, disabled, or medically fragile adults with volunteer dentists and labs for comprehensive dental care at no cost. Founded in 1975 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado. It operates primarily through its Donated Dental Services (DDS) program. Serving individuals in every state and Washington, D.C. Through July 2026, nearly 175,000 patients had received almost $586 million in total care from a volunteer network of 11,300 dentists and 3,033 labs. For more information, visit dentallifeline.org.
